what:
Study 1, radio. The coordinated mission on the same seeds with
  - packet loss p in {0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.95}: every (message, receiver) pair is
    dropped independently with probability p;
  - a range limit R in {5, 3} m: a message reaches a receiver only if the two
    robots are within R at send time;
  - the independent mode (bus off) as the floor.
The loss draws are common random numbers: one uniform per (message, receiver) is
drawn whatever p is, so a packet dropped at p = 0.5 is also dropped at p = 0.8
for as long as the two runs are still sending the same messages.
notes: Every mission ran commit 928f08ffad0061d4ac155705adbb4e8f4c09eb2b from a `git archive` of that commit unpacked outside the repo, so later commits could not move the code under the study. Module hashes are in each job header. fleet_search.py, fleet_sim.py, fleet_reflex.py, g1_collision.py and g1_newton.py are unchanged between 928f08f and 13a0341 (HEAD when this was written).

Seeds 40 to 51, 12 per cell, the same seeds in every cell. Slip reflex on unless the cell says otherwise. Physics is deterministic: there is no run-to-run noise, but a small change in what the agents do moves who meets which ice, so compare cells by paired seeds and not by one mission.
t_located / t_assembled medians are over the missions that succeeded only.
robot_metres is the summed path length of standing robots from Mission.track (5 Hz samples), so it includes body sway.
Earlier runs of these studies on the previous planners (e842003+wip, 2f8a232, deb3497, 3d637f3) are not in this file. deb3497 and 3d637f3 had route() bugs and their missions were discarded.
Loss draws are common random numbers across loss rates: one uniform per (message, receiver), drawn whatever p is.
LossyBus(loss=0, range=None) against fleet_search.Bus: 'loss 0' here and 'n=4 coordinated' in fleet_scale.json are the same 12 seeds, one through LossyBus and one through the stock Bus.

Cells named '+memory', '+patient', '+steady', '+relay' replace the stock RobotAgent with LongMemoryAgent, PatientAgent, SteadyAgent, RelayAgent from fleet_comms.py. The '+steady' cells were run by a later copy of fleet_comms.py (same simulator and agent modules) that adds that class.

slot conflict: two helpers whose claimed dig positions are under 0.86 m apart (the same position or neighbours; a legal pair is 1.1 m apart). Positions are compared, not slot indices, because each helper measures from its own idea of the centre.
bounce: one robot setting off the slip reflex three or more times on the same patch.
